name: Lip flip (Botox)
lead: A lip flip is a cosmetic procedure in which small amounts of botulinum toxin type A are injected into the muscle around the mouth, the orbicularis oris, along the upper lip border. Practitioners describe the aim as relaxing the muscle so the upper lip rolls slightly outward and upward, showing a little more of the pink lip without adding volume [1][2].

The technique is an off-label use of botulinum toxin. Published literature consists mainly of technique descriptions, case series and reviews, including a 2021 case series, a 2025 systematic review, and a 2026 study of clinical outcomes and the neuromuscular basis of upper lip eversion [1][3][4][5]. Effects are described as temporary and as lasting a few months [6].

In looksmaxxing communities, the lip flip is discussed as a low-cost way to make a thin upper lip look fuller or to alter lip proportions. The term is also used in the medical literature for different procedures, such as a hyaluronic acid filler technique reported in a 2022 study [7].
infobox: No, per descriptions of the technique

paras: The upper lip is encircled by the orbicularis oris, a sphincter-like muscle. In a lip flip, a clinician places small injections of botulinum toxin into the upper lip near the border of the vermilion. Reviews describe the intended results as improved contour, eversion and apparent fullness of the lip [1].

Because the toxin weakens muscle rather than adding material, descriptions stress that it changes how the lip sits rather than its volume. A summary on Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, says effects appear within one to two weeks and last three to four months, and that the technique can also reduce the look of a gummy smile [6]. That page is treated as unverified.

The phrase "lip flip" is not used consistently. One 2022 paper uses it for a perioral rejuvenation method based on hyaluronic acid filler placed with a cannula, evaluated in 70 women [7]. Most other literature uses it for the botulinum toxin technique [1][4]. Gelada monkeys also have a facial display called a lip-flip, which is unrelated [8].

Published human data are limited and mostly descriptive. A 2021 article in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery reviewed botulinum toxin for lip augmentation and noted that results and techniques for related uses such as gummy smile and perioral lines are better described than for the lip flip itself [1]. A 2021 case series and discussion examined the neurotoxin lip flip in patients [3]. A 2025 systematic review in Archives of Dermatological Research collected the studies on botulinum toxin lip augmentation [4]. A 2026 study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery reported clinical outcomes and discussed the neuromuscular basis of upper lip eversion [5], and a 2026 paper in Toxicon proposed a concept of balance between risorius and orbicularis oris for lip widening [9]. Researchers have also compared public search interest in lip filler and lip flip [10]. Comparative trials against fillers are not described in the sources reviewed.

Botulinum toxin injected near the mouth can affect nearby muscles; authors of the clinical literature discuss asymmetry and effects on speech, drinking and smiling as the kind of functional issues that can follow weakening of the orbicularis oris [1][4]. Specific rates are not given in the abstracts available.

Users on looksmax.org have written guides describing the lip flip as targeting a thin upper lip, a long philtrum and facial proportions such as facial width-to-height ratio and chin-to-philtrum ratio, and as a way to rebalance a crooked lip [11]. Some threads also discuss obtaining botulinum toxin outside clinics; the wiki does not summarise those. Medical sources describe the procedure as one done by clinicians [1].

timeline.event: Case series and review articles on the neurotoxin lip flip are published in dermatology and craniofacial journals.[1][3]
A separate "lip flip" filler technique for perioral rejuvenation is reported.[7]
A systematic review of botulinum toxin lip augmentation is published.[4]
A study of clinical outcomes and the neuromodulatory basis of upper lip eversion is published.[5]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the lip flip appears in guides as an inexpensive, reversible option for upper-lip proportions.[11]

claims.claim: A lip flip can make a thin upper lip look fuller and change facial proportions.
claims.believers: A forum guide says the injections roll the lip upward and outward and lists benefits such as improved lip proportions, a more compact midface, an apparently shorter philtrum and a better chin-to-philtrum ratio.[11]
claims.experts: Clinical papers describe improved contour, eversion and fullness, but the evidence is case series and reviews rather than controlled trials.[1][3][4]

claims.claim: The effect is temporary and reversible.
claims.believers: Forum users present it as a low-commitment trial of how a different lip shape would look.[11]
claims.experts: Descriptions of the technique state effects are temporary and wear off over a few months.[6]

claims.claim: The injection can be self-administered at home.
claims.believers: Forum threads discuss doing it themselves.[11]
claims.experts: The published literature describes the procedure as performed by clinicians and discusses the anatomical balance of the muscles around the mouth.[1][9]

card.summary: Botox in the upper lip muscle to roll the lip out; temporary, with only small studies behind it.
card.note: Off-label use; the term "lip flip" is also used for a filler technique.

quick.overview:
A lip flip uses small injections of botulinum toxin around the upper lip so it rolls slightly outward, showing a bit more pink lip without adding volume.

Evidence consists of case series, reviews and a 2025 systematic review. Forum users discuss it as a reversible way to change a thin upper lip.
quick.mechanism: Botulinum toxin weakens part of the orbicularis oris muscle, so the lip border everts and the lip looks fuller. Effects are described as lasting about three to four months.
quick.risks: Off-label use. Weakening muscles near the mouth can affect symmetry and function; published abstracts give no firm complication rates. Medical sources describe it as clinician-performed.
